content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us adore.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

Regem Apostolórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.

segments.t: Ant.
Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 18:2 Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.
content.english: 18:2 The heavens shew forth the glory of God, * and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.

segments.t: Cæli enárrant glóriam Dei: * et ópera mánuum eius annúntiat firmaméntum.

content.latin: 18:3 Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.
content.english: 18:3 Day to day uttereth speech, * and night to night sheweth knowledge.

segments.t: Dies diéi erúctat verbum, * et nox nocti índicat sciéntiam.

content.latin: 18:4 Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.
content.english: 18:4 There are no speeches nor languages, * where their voices are not heard.

segments.t: Non sunt loquélæ, neque sermónes, * quorum non audiántur voces eórum.

content.latin: 18:5 In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: 18:5 Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: * and their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: 18:6 In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:
content.english: 18:6 He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: * and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber,

segments.t: In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum: * et ipse tamquam sponsus procédens de thálamo suo:

content.latin: 18:6 Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:
content.english: 18:6 Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way: * his going out is from the end of heaven,

segments.t: Exsultávit ut gigas ad curréndam viam, * a summo cælo egréssio eius:

content.latin: 18:7 Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.
content.english: 18:7 And his circuit even to the end thereof: * and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.

segments.t: Et occúrsus eius usque ad summum eius: * nec est qui se abscóndat a calóre eius.

content.latin: 18:8 Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.
content.english: 18:8 The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: * the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.

segments.t: Lex Dómini immaculáta, convértens ánimas: * testimónium Dómini fidéle, sapiéntiam præstans párvulis.

content.latin: 18:9 Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.
content.english: 18:9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: * the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.

segments.t: Iustítiæ Dómini rectæ, lætificántes corda: * præcéptum Dómini lúcidum, illúminans óculos.

content.latin: 18:10 Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.
content.english: 18:10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: * the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.

segments.t: Timor Dómini sanctus, pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi: * iudícia Dómini vera, iustificáta in semetípsa.

content.latin: 18:11 Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.
content.english: 18:11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: * and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.

segments.t: Desiderabília super aurum et lápidem pretiósum multum: * et dulcióra super mel et favum.

content.latin: 18:12 Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.
content.english: 18:12 For thy servant keepeth them, * and in keeping them there is a great reward.

segments.t: Étenim servus tuus custódit ea, * in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa.

content.latin: 18:13 Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
content.english: 18:13 Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord: * and from those of others spare thy servant.

segments.t: Delícta quis intéllegit? ab occúltis meis munda me: * et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.

content.latin: 18:14 Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.
content.english: 18:14 If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: * and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.

segments.t: Si mei non fúerint domináti, tunc immaculátus ero: * et emundábor a delícto máximo.

content.latin: 18:15 Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.
content.english: 18:15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: * and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight.

segments.t: Et erunt ut compláceant elóquia oris mei: * et meditátio cordis mei in conspéctu tuo semper.

content.latin: 18:15 Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.
content.english: 18:15 O Lord, my helper, * and my redeemer.

segments.t: Dómine, adiútor meus, * et redémptor meus.

content.latin: Psalmus 33 [2]
content.english: Psalm 33 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 33

content.latin: 33:2 Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.
content.english: 33:2 I will bless the Lord at all times, * his praise shall be always in my mouth.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum in omni témpore: * semper laus eius in ore meo.

content.latin: 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.
content.english: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

segments.t: In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.

content.latin: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.
content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

segments.t: Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

segments.t: Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.

content.latin: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

segments.t: Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.

content.latin: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.
content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

segments.t: Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.

content.latin: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

segments.t: Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.

content.latin: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

segments.t: Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

segments.t: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

segments.t: Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

segments.t: Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

segments.t: Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

segments.t: Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

segments.t: Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

segments.t: Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

segments.t: Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.

content.latin: 33:18 Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

segments.t: Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.

content.latin: 33:19 Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
content.english: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

segments.t: Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.

content.latin: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

segments.t: Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

segments.t: Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

segments.t: Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

segments.t: Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.

content.english: Psalm 44 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 44

content.latin: 44:2 Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.
content.english: 44:2 My heart hath uttered a good word; * I speak my works to the King.

segments.t: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum: * dico ego ópera mea Regi.

content.latin: 44:2 Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.
content.english: 44:2 My tongue is the pen of a scrivener * that writeth swiftly.

segments.t: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ: * velóciter scribéntis.

content.latin: 44:3 Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 44:3 Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; * therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.

segments.t: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis: * proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.

content.latin: 44:4 Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.
content.english: 44:4 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, * O thou most mighty.

segments.t: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, * potentíssime.

content.latin: 44:5 Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
content.english: 44:5 With thy comeliness and thy beauty * set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

segments.t: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua: * inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.

content.latin: 44:5 Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
content.english: 44:5 Because of truth and meekness and justice: * and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

segments.t: Propter veritátem, et mansuetúdinem, et iustítiam: * et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.

content.latin: 44:6 Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.
content.english: 44:6 Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, * into the hearts of the king’s enemies.

segments.t: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent: * in corda inimicórum Regis.

content.latin: 44:7 Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.
content.english: 44:7 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: * the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

segments.t: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi: * virga directiónis virga regni tui.

content.latin: 44:8 Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
content.english: 44:8 Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: * therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

segments.t: Dilexísti iustítiam, et odísti iniquitátem: * proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.

content.latin: 44:9 Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
content.english: 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: * out of which the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory.

segments.t: Myrrha, et gutta, et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis: * ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.

content.latin: 44:10 Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.
content.english: 44:10 The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; * surrounded with variety.

segments.t: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto: * circúmdata varietáte.

content.latin: 44:11 Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
content.english: 44:11 Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: * and forget thy people and thy father’s house.

segments.t: Audi fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam: * et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.

content.latin: 44:12 Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
content.english: 44:12 And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; * for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.

segments.t: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum: * quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.

content.latin: 44:13 Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.
content.english: 44:13 And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, * yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

segments.t: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus * vultum tuum deprecabúntur: omnes dívites plebis.

content.latin: 44:14 Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.
content.english: 44:14 All the glory of the king’s daughter is within, * in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

segments.t: Omnis glória eius fíliæ Regis ab intus, * in fímbriis áureis circumamícta varietátibus.

content.latin: 44:15 Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.
content.english: 44:15 After her shall virgins be brought to the king: * her neighbours shall be brought to thee.

segments.t: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam: * próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

content.latin: 44:16 Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.
content.english: 44:16 They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: * they shall be brought into the temple of the king.

segments.t: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne: * adducéntur in templum Regis.

content.latin: 44:17 Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
content.english: 44:17 Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: * thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

segments.t: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii: * constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.

content.latin: 44:18 Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
content.english: 44:18 They shall remember thy name * throughout all generations.

segments.t: Mémores erunt nóminis tui: * in omni generatióne et generatiónem.

content.latin: 44:18 Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 44:18 Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, * for ever and ever.

segments.t: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum: * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth. They shall remember thy name, O Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram: mémores erunt nóminis tui, Dómine.

content.latin: ℣. In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.
content.english: ℣. Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth:

segments.t: In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.
content.english: ℟. And their words unto the ends of the world.

segments.t: Et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Incipit Epístola cathólica beáti Iudæ Apóstoli
content.english: Beginning of the letter of the blessed Apostle Jude

content.latin: Iudas 1:1-4
content.english: Jude 1:1-4

segments.t: Iudas 1:1-4

content.latin: 1 Iudas, Iesu Christi servus, frater autem Iacóbi, his qui sunt in Deo Patre diléctis, et Christo Iesu conservátis, et vocátis.
content.english: 1 Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James: to them that are beloved in God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called.

segments.t: Iudas, Iesu Christi servus, frater autem Iacóbi, his qui sunt in Deo Patre diléctis, et Christo Iesu conservátis, et vocátis.

content.latin: 2 Misericórdia vobis, et pax, et cáritas adimpleátur.
content.english: 2 Mercy unto you, and peace, and charity be fulfilled.

segments.t: Misericórdia vobis, et pax, et cáritas adimpleátur.

content.latin: 3 Caríssimi, omnem sollicitúdinem fáciens scribéndi vobis de commúni vestra salúte, necésse hábui scríbere vobis: déprecans supercertári semel tráditæ sanctis fídei.
content.english: 3 Dearly beloved, taking all care to write unto you concerning your common salvation, I was under a necessity to write unto you: to beseech you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.

segments.t: Caríssimi, omnem sollicitúdinem fáciens scribéndi vobis de commúni vestra salúte, necésse hábui scríbere vobis: déprecans supercertári semel tráditæ sanctis fídei.

content.latin: 4 Subintroiérunt enim quidam hómines (qui olim præscrípti sunt in hoc iudícium) ímpii, Dei nostri grátiam transferéntes in luxúriam, et solum Dominatórem, et Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum negántes.
content.english: 4 For certain men are secretly entered in, (who were written of long ago unto this judgment,) ungodly men, turning the grace of our Lord God into riotousness, and denying the only sovereign Ruler, and our Lord Jesus Christ.

segments.t: Subintroiérunt enim quidam hómines (qui olim præscrípti sunt in hoc iudícium) ímpii, Dei nostri grátiam transferéntes in luxúriam, et solum Dominatórem, et Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum negántes.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:
content.english: ℟. Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves, said the Lord:

segments.t: Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oves in médio lupórum, dicit Dóminus:

content.latin: * Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
content.english: * Be ye, therefore, wise as serpents and simple as doves.

content.latin: ℣. Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.
content.english: ℣. Whilst you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be the children of light.

segments.t: Dum lucem habétis, crédite in lucem, ut fílii lucis sitis.

content.latin: ℟. Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.
content.english: ℟. Be ye therefore wise as serpents and simple as doves.

segments.t: Estóte ergo prudéntes sicut serpéntes, et símplices sicut colúmbæ.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Iudas 1:5-8
content.english: Jude 1:5-8

segments.t: Iudas 1:5-8

content.latin: 5 Commonére autem vos volo, sciéntes semel ómnia, quóniam Iesus pópulum de terra Ægýpti salvans, secúndo eos, qui non credidérunt, pérdidit:
content.english: 5 I will therefore admonish you, though ye once knew all things, that Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not:

segments.t: Commonére autem vos volo, sciéntes semel ómnia, quóniam Iesus pópulum de terra Ægýpti salvans, secúndo eos, qui non credidérunt, pérdidit:

content.latin: 6 Ángelos vero, qui non servavérunt suum principátum, sed dereliquérunt suum domicílium, in iudícium magni diéi, vínculis ætérnis sub calígine reservávit.
content.english: 6 And the angels who kept not their principality, but forsook their own habitation, he hath reserved under darkness in everlasting chains, unto the judgment of the great day.

segments.t: Ángelos vero, qui non servavérunt suum principátum, sed dereliquérunt suum domicílium, in iudícium magni diéi, vínculis ætérnis sub calígine reservávit.

content.latin: 7 Sicut Sódoma, et Gomórrha, et finítimæ civitátes símili modo exfornicátæ, et abeúntes post carnem álteram, factæ sunt exémplum, ignis ætérni pœnam sustinéntes.
content.english: 7 As Sodom and Gomorrha, and the neighbouring cities, in like manner, having given themselves to fornication, and going after other flesh, were made an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.

segments.t: Sicut Sódoma, et Gomórrha, et finítimæ civitátes símili modo exfornicátæ, et abeúntes post carnem álteram, factæ sunt exémplum, ignis ætérni pœnam sustinéntes.

content.latin: 8 Simíliter et hi carnem quidem máculant, dominatiónem autem spernunt, maiestátem autem blasphémant.
content.english: 8 In like manner these men also defile the flesh, and despise dominion, and blaspheme majesty.

segments.t: Simíliter et hi carnem quidem máculant, dominatiónem autem spernunt, maiestátem autem blasphémant.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Tóllite iugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:
content.english: ℟. Take up my yoke upon you, said the Lord, and learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart.

segments.t: Tóllite iugum meum super vos, dicit Dóminus, et díscite a me, quia mitis sum et húmilis corde:

content.latin: * Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
content.english: * For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

content.latin: ℣. Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.
content.english: ℣. And you shall find rest to your souls.

segments.t: Et inveniétis réquiem animábus vestris.

content.latin: ℟. Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.
content.english: ℟. For my yoke is sweet and my burden light.

segments.t: Iugum enim meum suáve est, et onus meum leve.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Iudas 1:9-13
content.english: Jude 1:9-13

segments.t: Iudas 1:9-13

content.latin: 9 Cum Míchael Archángelus cum diábolo dísputans altercarétur de Móysi córpore, non est ausus iudícium inférre blasphémiæ: sed dixit: Imperet tibi Dóminus.
content.english: 9 When Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, contended about the body of Moses, he durst not bring against him the judgment of railing speech, but said: The Lord command thee.

segments.t: Cum Míchael Archángelus cum diábolo dísputans altercarétur de Móysi córpore, non est ausus iudícium inférre blasphémiæ: sed dixit: Imperet tibi Dóminus.

content.latin: 10 Hi autem quæcúmque quidem ignórant, blasphémant: quæcúmque autem naturáliter, tamquam muta animália, norunt, in his corrumpúntur.
content.english: 10 But these men blaspheme whatever things they know not: and what things soever they naturally know, like dumb beasts, in these they are corrupted.

segments.t: Hi autem quæcúmque quidem ignórant, blasphémant: quæcúmque autem naturáliter, tamquam muta animália, norunt, in his corrumpúntur.

content.latin: 11 Væ illis, quia in via Cain abiérunt, et erróre Bálaam mercéde effúsi sunt, et in contradictióne Core periérunt!
content.english: 11 Woe unto them, for they have gone in the way of Cain: and after the error of Balaam they have for reward poured out themselves, and have perished in the contradiction of Core.

segments.t: Væ illis, quia in via Cain abiérunt, et erróre Bálaam mercéde effúsi sunt, et in contradictióne Core periérunt!

content.latin: 12 Hi sunt in épulis suis máculæ, convivántes sine timóre, semetípsos pascéntes, nubes sine aqua, quæ a ventis circumferéntur, árbores autumnáles, infructuósæ, bis mórtuæ, eradicátæ,
content.english: 12 These are spots in their banquets, feasting together without fear, feeding themselves, clouds without water, which are carried about by winds, trees of the autumn, unfruitful, twice dead, plucked up by the roots,

segments.t: Hi sunt in épulis suis máculæ, convivántes sine timóre, semetípsos pascéntes, nubes sine aqua, quæ a ventis circumferéntur, árbores autumnáles, infructuósæ, bis mórtuæ, eradicátæ,

content.latin: 13 Fluctus feri maris, despumántes suas confusiónes, sídera errántia: quibus procélla tenebrárum serváta est in ætérnum.
content.english: 13 Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own confusion; wandering stars, to whom the storm of darkness is reserved for ever.

segments.t: Fluctus feri maris, despumántes suas confusiónes, sídera errántia: quibus procélla tenebrárum serváta est in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:
content.english: ℟. But when they shall deliver you up to the judges, take no thought how or what to speak:

segments.t: Dum stetéritis ante reges et prǽsides, nolíte cogitáre quómodo aut quid loquámini:

content.latin: * Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: * for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak:

content.latin: ℣. Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.
content.english: ℣. For it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father that speaketh in you.

segments.t: Non enim vos estis qui loquímini: sed Spíritus Patris vestri, qui lóquitur in vobis.

content.latin: ℟. Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.
content.english: ℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

segments.t: Dábitur enim vobis in illa hora, quid loquámini.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. For it shall be given you in that hour what to speak.

content.english: Ant. The princes of the people * are gathered together, with the God of Abraham.

Príncipes populórum * congregáti sunt cum Deo Ábraham.

content.latin: Psalmus 46 [4]
content.english: Psalm 46 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 46

content.latin: Scriptum est: Spíritus Dómini ornávit cælos. Ornaménta enim cælórum sunt virtútes prædicántium. Quæ vidélicet ornaménta Paulus enúmerat, dicens: Álii datur per Spíritum sermo sapiéntiæ, álii sermo sciéntiæ secúndum eúndem Spíritum, álteri fides in eódem Spíritu, álii grátia sanitátum in uno Spíritu, álii operátio virtútum, álii prophetía, álii discrétio spirítuum, álii génera linguárum, álii interpretátio sermónum. Hæc autem ómnia operátur unus atque idem Spíritus, dívidens síngulis prout vult.
content.english: It is written: By His Spirit the Lord hath adorned the heavens. Job xxvi. 13. Now the ornament of the heavens are the godly powers of preachers, and this ornament, what it is, Paul teacheth us thus To one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom, to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; to another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discerning of spirits, to another diverse kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. But all these worketh that one and the self-same Spirit, dividing to every man severally as He will. 1 Cor. xii. 8.

content.latin: Quot ergo sunt bona prædicántium, tot sunt ornaménta cælórum. Hinc rursus scriptum est: Verbo Dómini cæli firmáti sunt. Verbum enim Dómini Fílius est Patris. Sed eósdem cælos, vidélicet sanctos Apóstolos, ut tota simul sancta Trínitas ostendátur operáta, repénte de Sancti Spíritus divinitáte adiúngitur: Et Spíritu oris eius omnis virtus eórum. Cælórum ergo virtus de Spíritu sumpta est: quia mundi huius potestátibus contraíre non præsúmerent, nisi eos Sancti Spíritus fortitúdo solidásset. Quales namque doctóres sanctæ Ecclésiæ ante advéntum huius Spíritus fúerint, scimus: et post advéntum illíus, cuius fortitúdinis facti sint, conspícimus.
content.english: So much power then as have preachers, so much ornament have the heavens. Wherefore again it is written By the word of the Lord were the heavens made. ~Ps. xxxii. 6. For the Word of the Lord is the Son of the Father. But, to the end that all the Holy Trinity may be made manifest as the Maker of the heavens, that is, of the Apostles, it is straightway added touching God the Holy Ghost: you and all the host of them by the Breath of His mouth. Therefore the might of the same heavens is the might of the Spirit, for they had not braved the powers of this world, unless the strength of the Holy Ghost had comforted them. For we know what manner of men the Teachers of the Holy Church were before the coming of this Spirit and since He came we see in Whose strength they are made strong.

content.latin: In lectióne evangélica quæ hanc antecédit, díxerat Dóminus: Non vos me elegístis; sed ego elégi vos et pósui vos, ut eátis, et fructum afferátis, et fructus vester máneat: ut quodcúmque petiéritis Patrem in nómine meo, det vobis. Hic autem dicit: Hæc mando vobis, ut diligátis ínvicem. Ac per hoc intellégere debémus hunc esse fructum nostrum, de quo ait: Ego vos elégi, ut eátis, et fructum afferátis, et fructus vester máneat. Et quod adiúnxit, Ut quodcúmque petiéritis Patrem in nómine meo, det vobis, tunc útique dabit nobis, si diligámus ínvicem; cum et hoc ipsum ipse déderit nobis, qui nos elégit non habéntes fructum, quia non eum nos elegerámus, et pósuit nos ut fructum afferámus, hoc est, ínvicem diligámus.
content.english: In the reading from the Gospel, the last before this, the Lord had said: Ye have not chosen Me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go, and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in My Name, He may give it you. And here He saith: These things I command you, that ye love one another. And by this it is that we must understand what fruit from us it is, whereof He saith: I have chosen, that ye should go, and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain, and so the words added That whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in My Name, He may give it you. He will give unto us when we love one another, since this (mutual love) is itself the gift of Him Who hath chosen us when as yet we were fruitless, since it hath not been we who have chosen Him, (but He Who hath chosen us,) and ordained us, that we should go, and bring forth fruit, that is to say, should love one another.

content.latin: Cáritas ergo est fructus noster, quam defínit Apóstolus, De corde puro, et consciéntia bona, et fide non ficta. Hac dilígimus ínvicem, hac dilígimus Deum; neque enim vera dilectióne diligerémus ínvicem, nisi diligéntes Deum. Díligit enim unusquísque próximum suum tamquam seípsum, si díligit Deum. Nam, si non díligit Deum, non díligit seípsum; in his enim duóbus præcéptis caritátis tota lex pendet et prophétæ. Hic est fructus noster. De fructu ítaque nobis mandans, Hæc mando, inquit, vobis, ut diligátis ínvicem. Unde et Apóstolus Paulus, cum contra ópera carnis commendáre fructum spíritus vellet, a cápite hoc pósuit: Fructus, inquit, spíritus, cáritas est; ac deínde cétera, tamquam ex isto cápite exórta et religáta contéxuit, quæ sunt, gáudium, pax, longanímitas, benígnitas, bónitas, fides, mansuetúdo, continéntia, cástitas.
content.english: Love then, is the fruit which we should bring forth, and the Apostle Paul telleth us 1 Tim. i. 5 that this love is love out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned. This is the love wherewith we love our neighbour, the love wherewith we love God, for we do not really love our neighbour unless we love God. For if any man love God, he loveth his neighbour as himself, since he that loveth not God loveth not himself. For on these two commandments hangeth all the law and the Prophets. Love, then, is the fruit which we should bring forth. And concerning this fruit, the Lord giveth us this commandment: These things (saith He) I command you, that ye love one another. Hence also the Apostle Paul Gal. v. 22 when he is about praising up the fruits of the Spirit as opposed to the works of the flesh, saith first of all: The fruit of the Spirit is love. And from that as the beginning he draweth out a string of other fruits, as thence begotten and thereto bound, namely, joy, peace, long-suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance, chastity.

content.latin: Quis autem bene gaudet, qui bonum non díligit unde gaudet? Quis pacem veram, nisi cum illo potest habére, quem veráciter díligit? Quis est longánimis in bono ópere perseveránter manéndo, nisi férveat diligéndo? Quis est benígnus, nisi díligat cui opitulátur? Quis bonus, nisi diligéndo efficiátur? Quis salúbriter fidélis, nisi ea fide quæ per dilectiónem operátur? Quis utíliter mansuétus, cui non diléctio moderétur? Quis ab eo cóntinet unde turpátur, nisi díligat unde honestátur? Mérito ítaque Magíster bonus dilectiónem sic sæpe comméndat, tamquam sola præcipiénda sit, sine qua non possunt prodésse cétera bona, et quæ non potest habéri sine céteris bonis, quibus homo effícitur bonus.
content.english: Who is really joyful that loveth not the cause of his joy? Who can really be at one with another, unless he loveth that other? Who is cheerful under long toil for a good work, unless he loveth the aim? Who is kind, unless he love the object of his tenderness? Who is good, unless by the persuasion of love? Who is truly faithful, unless by the faith which worketh by love? Who is gentle to any use, unless love move him? Who turneth away from baseness unless he love honour? Well, then, doth the Good Master so often command us to love, as though that commandment were all-sufficient, for love is that gift without which all other good things avail nothing, and which cannot be without having every other good gift which maketh a good man good.

content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:)
Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

Beáti pacífici, beáti mundo corde: quóniam ipsi Deum vidébunt.

content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 148

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

segments.t: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. In patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.
content.english: Ant. In your patience you shall possess your souls.

In patiéntia vestra possidébitis ánimas vestras.

content.latin: Fratres: Iam non estis hóspites et ádvenæ: sed estis cives Sanctórum et doméstici Dei: superædificáti super fundaméntum Apostolórum, et Prophetárum, ipso summo angulári lápide Christo Iesu.
content.english: Brothers: Now therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners; but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and the domestics of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

segments.t: Hymnus

content.latin: Exsúltet orbis gáudiis:
content.english: Now let the earth with joy resound,

content.latin: Cælum resúltet láudibus:
content.english: And heaven the chant re-echo round;

content.latin: Apostolórum glóriam
content.english: Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise

content.latin: Tellus et astra cóncinunt.
content.english: The great Apostles' glorious praise.

content.latin: Vos sæculórum iúdices,
content.english: O ye who, throned in glory dread,

content.latin: Et vera mundi lúmina:
content.english: Shall judge the living and the dead,

content.latin: Votis precámur córdium,
content.english: Lights of the world forevermore!

content.latin: Audíte voces súpplicum.
content.english: To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

content.latin: Qui templa cæli cláuditis,
content.english: Ye close the sacred gates on high;

content.latin: Serásque verbo sólvitis,
content.english: At your command apart they fly:

content.latin: Nos a reátu nóxios
content.english: Oh! loose for us the guilty chain

content.latin: Solvi iubéte, quǽsumus.
content.english: We strive to break, and strive in vain.

content.latin: Præcépta quorum prótinus
content.english: Sickness and health your voice obey;

content.latin: Languor salúsque séntiunt:
content.english: At your command they go or stay:

content.latin: Sanáte mentes lánguidas:
content.english: From sin's disease our souls restore;

content.latin: Augéte nos virtútibus.
content.english: In good confirm us more and more.

content.latin: Ut, cum redíbit árbiter
content.english: So when the world is at its end,

content.latin: In fine Christus sǽculi,
content.english: And Christ to judgement shall descend,

content.latin: Nos sempitérni gáudii
content.english: May we be called those joys to see

content.latin: Concédat esse cómpotes.
content.english: Prepared from all eternity.

content.latin: Patri, simúlque Fílio,
content.english: Praise to the Father, with the Son,

content.latin: Tibíque Sancte Spíritus,
content.english: And Holy Spirit, Three in One;

content.latin: Sicut fuit, sit iúgiter
content.english: As ever was in ages past,

content.latin: Sæclum per omne glória.
content.english: And so shall be while ages last.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Annuntiavérunt ópera Dei.
content.english: ℣. They declared the works of God.

segments.t: Annuntiavérunt ópera Dei.

content.latin: ℟. Et facta eius intellexérunt.
content.english: ℟. And understood his doings.

segments.t: Et facta eius intellexérunt.

content.english: Ant. You who left all * and follow me, you will receive hundredfolds, and you will have eternal life.

segments.t: Ant.
Vos qui reliquístis * ómnia, et secúti estis me, céntuplum accipiétis, et vitam ætérnam possidébitis.

content.english: Canticle of Zacharias

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

segments.t: Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: 25:1 Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
content.english: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

segments.t: Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.

content.latin: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
content.english: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

segments.t: Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.

content.latin: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
content.english: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

segments.t: Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.

content.latin: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
content.english: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

segments.t: Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.

content.latin: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
content.english: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

segments.t: Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.

content.latin: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
content.english: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

segments.t: Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:

content.latin: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
content.english: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.

content.latin: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

segments.t: Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.

content.latin: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:

segments.t: Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:

content.latin: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.

segments.t: In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.

segments.t: Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.

content.latin: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
content.english: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

segments.t: Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?

content.english: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

segments.t: Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.

segments.t: Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.

content.latin: 51:8 Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:

segments.t: Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.

segments.t: Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.

content.latin: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
content.english: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

segments.t: Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.

segments.t: Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.

content.latin: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

segments.t: Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

content.latin: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?

segments.t: Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?

content.latin: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.

segments.t: Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.

segments.t: Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.

content.latin: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
content.english: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

content.english: Upon the same day, the holy Bishops Maximilian the martyr, and Valentine the Confessor.

content.latin: Hierosólymis natális beáti Narcíssi Epíscopi, sanctitáte, patiéntia ac fide laudábilis, qui, centum et séxdecim annórum senex, felíciter migrávit ad Dóminum.
content.english: At Bergamo, the holy Virgin and martyr Eusebia.

content.latin: Augustodúni sancti Ioánnis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
content.english: At Jerusalem, the blessed Narcissus, Bishop (of that see,) praiseworthy for his holiness, his long-suffering, and his faith, who at the age of one hundred and sixteen years passed away to be ever with the Lord.

content.latin: Cassíope, in ínsula Corcýra, sancti Donáti Epíscopi, de quo scribit beátus Gregórius Papa.
content.english: At Autun, the holy Confessor the Bishop John.

content.latin: Viénnæ, in Gállia, deposítio beáti Theodóri Abbátis.
content.english: At Cassiope, in the island of Corfu, holy Donatus, of whom writeth blessed Pope Gregory.

content.latin: ℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
content.english: At Vienne, (in the sixth century,) deceased the blessed Theodore, Abbot (of the monastery founded by him in honour of the Blessed Virgin, but commonly called after himself.)

segments.t: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℣. Precious in the sight of the Lord

content.english: ℟. Is the death of his saints.

content.latin: Sancta María et omnes Sancti intercédant pro nobis ad Dóminum, ut nos mereámur ab eo adiuvári et salvári, qui vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Holy Mary and all the Saints, intercede for us with the Lord, our God, so that we may merit His help and salvation, who lives and reigns for ever and ever.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Kýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
content.english: Lord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.
content.english: ℣. Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.

segments.t: Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: ℟. And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

segments.t: Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.
content.english: Benediction. May Almighty God arrange our deeds and our day in His peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Dies et actus nostros in sua pace dispónat Dóminus omnípotens.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 2 Thess 3:5
content.english: 2 Thess 3:5

segments.t: 2 Thess 3:5

content.latin: Dóminus autem dírigat corda et córpora nostra in caritáte Dei et patiéntia Christi.
content.english: And the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℣. Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,

segments.t: Adiutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.

content.latin: ℟. Qui fecit cælum et terram.
content.english: ℟. Who made heaven and earth.

segments.t: Qui fecit cælum et terram.

content.latin: ℣. Benedícite.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless.

segments.t: Benedícite.

content.latin: ℟. Deus.
content.english: ℟. God.

segments.t: Deus.

content.latin: Benedictio. Dóminus nos benedícat, ✠ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Dóminus nos benedícat, ✠ et ab omni malo deféndat, et ad vitam perdúcat ætérnam. Et fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Nunc, Sancte, nobis, Spíritus,
content.english: Come Holy Ghost who ever One

content.latin: Unum Patri cum Fílio,
content.english: Art with the Father and the Son,

content.latin: Dignáre promptus íngeri
content.english: It is the hour, our souls possess

content.latin: Nostro refúsus péctori.
content.english: With thy full flood of holiness.

content.english: Let flesh and heart and lips and mind

content.english: Sound forth our witness to mankind;

content.latin: Flamméscat igne cáritas,
content.english: And love light up our mortal frame,

content.latin: Accéndat ardor próximos.
content.english: Till others catch the living flame.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
